prerequisites.name: bun >= 1.0
prerequisites.purpose: JavaScript runtime and package manager used by every script and the installer itself.

prerequisites.name: node >= 18
prerequisites.purpose: Your agent's hooks run on Node, so bun setup does not start without it; the npx wrapper of create-agentic-qa needs it too.

prerequisites.name: git
prerequisites.purpose: Clones the template and tracks your project's history. Set user.name and user.email before the first commit, or the preflight warns.

prerequisites.name: an AI agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex or Pi)
prerequisites.purpose: bun setup configures only the agents you pick, and does not start when none is installed.

prerequisites.name: internet access
prerequisites.purpose: Community skills download from the npm registry and GitHub, the test browser from cdn.playwright.dev; the preflight probes all three.

prerequisites.name: disk space (1.1 GB+)
prerequisites.purpose: Chromium and the dependencies use about 1.1 GB. Below 400 MB free bun setup does not start; below 1.2 GB it warns.

prerequisites.name: acli (Atlassian CLI)
prerequisites.purpose: The Jira phase signs in and syncs catalogs with it; without it the Jira phase is skipped.

prerequisites.name: engram >= 3.0
prerequisites.purpose: Cross-session memory for the agents; without it the memory step is skipped.

prerequisites.name: gh (GitHub CLI)
prerequisites.purpose: Only for the GitHub phase (create the remote repository and push); choose local only otherwise.

prerequisites.name: 1Password CLI (op)
prerequisites.purpose: Only when the project keeps its secrets in 1Password (secrets.provider: 1password).

prerequisites.name: Python 3.9+ with Pillow
prerequisites.purpose: Only for the evidence pages (/evidence-artifact, bun run evidence); nothing in the install needs it.
prerequisites.installHint: https://www.python.org/downloads/ then Pillow (Homebrew Python: brew install pillow; Windows: py -m pip install pillow)

prerequisites.name: API keys (.env)
prerequisites.purpose: The project MCP servers that read keys (slack-aurora, dbhub, openapi) connect once their values are in .env; web search and similar servers run at harness level and keep their keys outside .env.
prerequisites.installHint: See .env.example in the project root after scaffolding.

items.name: playwright-cli
items.purpose: Browser automation CLI — screenshots, traces, video, session management, request mocking.

items.name: playwright-best-practices
items.purpose: Playwright reference patterns — flaky-test fixes, POM, accessibility (axe-core), auth/OAuth fixtures, perf budgets, i18n, component testing.

items.name: skill-creator
items.purpose: Create, modify, and evaluate Claude Code skills.

items.name: diagram-design
items.purpose: Diagrams for the business context maps (data, API, E2E).

items.name: github-actions-docs
items.purpose: GitHub Actions documentation and workflow patterns.

items.name: mkd
items.purpose: Decision-deck CLI — the AI asks, the user answers point by point in a browser deck.

mcps.name: context7
mcps.purpose: Library documentation MCP — fetches official current docs for any library.

mcps.name: slack-aurora
mcps.purpose: Slack bot MCP — read channels, post and react from the agent (optional; token in .env).

mcps.name: dbhub
mcps.purpose: DBHub MCP — direct DB queries and schema introspection for test data validation.

mcps.name: openapi
mcps.purpose: OpenAPI MCP — explore API endpoints and contract testing from the agent.

envFiles.what: Created from .env.example. Stores all API keys and secrets (gitignored).
Already committed. Uses ${VAR} placeholders — installer ensures .env has the values.
Already committed. Uses {env:VAR} placeholders — installer ensures .env has the values.
Project identity, environments and the selected agents, written by the Team and Project phases.
Installer idempotency state (gitignored). Tracks which steps completed.

auth.method: Signed in by the Jira phase with the .env email and token — credentials stored in ~/.config/acli/. Site host from .agents/project.yaml (bun run jira:url --slug), not from the environment.

auth.service: Jira via the opt-in Atlassian MCP (HTTP basic auth)
auth.method: Not configured by bun setup: acli stays the default Jira path. When enabled, env vars are read at MCP startup; the site host is pasted into the config (an MCP config cannot run a command); print it with bun run jira:url.
Not configured by bun setup: credentials are read when a bun xray command runs. Only needed when the project uses Xray as its TMS.

steps.what: Checks tools, AI agents, network and disk in a few seconds (cli/preflight.ts). A blocking row stops the run before anything is written; a warning only skips the step it affects.
Asks once whether to start; --non-interactive skips it.
A project copied with "Use this template" gets a clean .agents/project.yaml from the schema before anything writes to it.
Which agents the project supports (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi), recorded in .agents/project.yaml `harnesses:`; the files of an agent you drop can be removed.
Detects Engram 3.0+ and, for Claude Code, offers its plugin (session hooks, installed once per machine).
Which user-level community skills to install, one by one; a declined skill is left out of later runs.
bun install when node_modules is missing or stale. Runs in the background while the next phases ask their questions.
Downloads the Playwright test browser (bunx playwright install chromium).
engram setup for each selected agent, plus the Claude Code plugin when accepted.
bunx skills add: project-level skills into .agents/skills/, the chosen user-level skills globally.
Repairs the agent contract: the .claude/skills alias onto .agents/skills/ and the CLAUDE.md shim.
Project name, key, web domain, local and staging URLs and the default environment, written to .agents/project.yaml by agents-setup --non-interactive (bun run agents:setup changes them later).
Offers to remove the .env keys this version no longer reads.
Where secret values live: .env (default) or 1Password, which writes the committed .env.provider.schema with references only.

Checks the variables each project MCP server reads and asks for the ones the installer manages. A value already set in your shell is copied into .env only when you say yes; an unattended run copies none and lists the names.
The Atlassian email and API token (and the other core variables) the skills use today; the rest is added when needed.
Optional bun run api:login, offered only when the test user and API_BASE_URL exist and the API answers.
Signs the Atlassian CLI in with the .env email and token; a rejected token is asked again.
Custom fields, workflows and link types, from your own Jira (workflow pickers through jira:sync-workflows --plan-json / --answers) or from the UPEX reference catalog; writes .agents/jira-*.json.
Right after the catalogs: offers the suggested board.statuses buckets once, then board.jql (default from the project key); written only when bun run board:check would accept the block.
bun run jira:check validates the Jira setup manifest against the synced catalogs.
Optional: creates the remote with gh (account, visibility, name) and pushes the first commit, after the background downloads finish.
Reports which external CLIs are on PATH (information only; nothing is installed).
Counts the project MCP servers that are ready and checks instructions, skills and MCP configs for every selected agent.
Retires the plaintext MCP credential copies an older install left behind.
Writes .template/installer.state.json so the next run repeats nothing.
One report: what was done, what is pending and what to run next.
